newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Conrail up after new bid.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Conrail up after new bid.

text.p: The bidding war for Conrail Inc between Norfolk Southern Corp and CSX Corp brought another sweetened offer for the railroad, this time from Norfolk, news that lifted Conrail shares before Friday's open.
Before the opening bell, Conrail shares rose to 95-1/2 from 93 as investors weighed Norfolk's $10 per share increase, raising the all cash bid to $110 per share.
Conrail had rejected the earlier unwelcome offer and Wednesday received a sweetened offer from friendly merger partner CSX.

On Wednesday, CSX raised to $100 per share from $92.50 its offer for the first 40 percent of Conrail shares tendered and left unchanged the second step stock-swap offer of 1.85619 CSX shares for each Conrail share.
Norfolk and CSX stock made no moves before the open, traders said.
Elsewhere, America Online Inc traded 1/4 down to 24-1/2 in the wake of a quarterly earnings report that included a $353.7 million net loss, or $3.80 per share.
The results for the fiscal first quarter ended September 30 included marketing expense write-off of $385.2 million.
Iomega Corp shares gained 1-3/4 to 25-3/4 preceding the market open as investors liked what many in the market consider the added appeal of a New York Stock Exchange listing.
Iomega will make its NYSE debut today, moving from the Nasdaq.
With an NYSE listing, traders said Iomega now will meet more of the investing criteria used by institutional stock buyers and mutual funds.
